# croaring / croaring_fuzzer

croaring's own fuzz target `croaring_fuzzer` ([source](source/croaring_fuzzer.c), modified; see below), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over CRoaring 5.1.0 (RoaringBitmap/CRoaring at 0489dd47).

Checks 2 properties (listed below); the first, an invariant: 32-bit: for a deserialised bitmap that passes roaring_bitmap_internal_validate, adding each absent value in [100,1000) must raise get_cardinality by exactly the number of values added (cardinality bookkeeping matches membership).

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against CRoaring 5.1.0 at commit 0489dd47 with 1 patch to the library (listed on the project page).
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.
- The harness source differs from the upstream file at the pinned commit; the copy in source/ is the file as built.

## What the harness checks
- 32-bit: for a deserialised bitmap that passes roaring_bitmap_internal_validate, adding each absent value in [100,1000) must raise get_cardinality by exactly the number of values added (cardinality bookkeeping matches membership) ([lines 42-53](source/croaring_fuzzer.c#L42-L53)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- same cardinality-after-add law on the roaring64 path ([lines 79-90](source/croaring_fuzzer.c#L79-L90)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch croaring` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| plain | `croaring_fuzzer.plain` | 74,720 | `0f3e6ebb663139023e2e68c5c11a84988d0f6626297fc3bfcc2688e64e2add25` |
| ubsan | `croaring_fuzzer.ubsan` | 85,096 | `b0a4e4b5165ca92d0c2d790524e7760311c8e31b670643a3e8b9f833de54c518` |
| asan | `croaring_fuzzer.asan` | 639,544 | `fcdb27fd0db3afd7d9f9e616ff5a96212e588ccf50e20a39e6ed6664f2e09787` |
| asan-ubsan | `croaring_fuzzer.asan-ubsan` | 650,168 | `48a5834d22a2fa8ebc8d3d0953c9452827752290bedf5c54906770be205e185a` |

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- asan-ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
